entries.title: INPUT PREPROCESSOR
entries.cause: Named file-return scenarios cover quoted filename bytes, percent substitution, first-line/EOF and empty fallback, exit status, secure and CLI policies, exact initial diagnostics and acknowledgment, foreground tty input and TERM cleanup. A leading dash extends execution and validation to stdin. The file-return form retains stdin regardless of the returned filename, and helper reads consume stdin. Named file/stdin transitions retain applicability, data and file-count prompts. Live pipes, LESSCLOSE, custom shell/metachar settings, repeated interactive diagnostics and interrupted/stopped helper interactions remain open. Real SIGINT cleanup and -K are covered; keyboard SIGINT still misses pager interrupt behavior while the helper owns a separate foreground group. File-return postprocessing covers normal exit, switches, binary refusal, stdin, empty fallback and quoted arguments; live-pipe cleanup and interactive invalid-template diagnostics remain open. Invalid-template diagnostics also cover file-switch acknowledgment, key replay and -K interrupts.

entries.title: SIGHUP terminal restoration divergence
entries.cause: Owner /yea approves retaining cleanup as an explicit safety divergence. The pinned oracle leaks represented modes on one-byte file then HUP; lz cleanup and signal death have independent safety proof. Retain strict mismatch and parity/S04c-hup. This choice does not establish equivalence or authorize oracle changes.

entries.title: Unknown and ambiguous CLI option diagnostics
entries.evidence: compatible in the named tested scenarios

entries.title: Long logical lines preserve complete UTF-8 content
entries.evidence: compatible in the named tested scenarios
entries.cause: Initial display uses bounded byte prefixes. Strict 16 MiB ASCII and UTF-8 first-screen scenarios pass. Source bytes remain in seekable files or anonymous spools, scanning uses 64 KiB blocks, and line offsets spill after 8192 entries. Whole-line search and wrapped navigation still materialize complete lines; open-producer PTY proof, RSS gates and exact malformed-byte display remain open.

entries.title: Empty and short files keep an interactive EOF view
entries.evidence: compatible in the named tested scenarios

entries.title: Refuse a binary file before acquiring the alternate screen

anchor.text: answer = query("\"%s\" may be a binary file.  See it anyway? ", &parg);

entries.evidence: compatible in the named tested scenarios
entries.cause: Under locale C, n/Enter refuse with code 1, uppercase Q quits with code 0 and TERM exits with code 15 on the primary screen. Accepting with y enters the alternate screen and displays six NUL bytes in inverse caret notation. Filename controls are printable; staged controls verify acquisition and cleanup. Other query interactions remain open.

entries.title: Binary sample thresholds use the resolved ASCII or UTF-8 character policy
entries.evidence: compatible in the named tested scenarios
entries.cause: Strict cases cover five versus six binary units, the 256-byte boundary, UTF-8 controls and malformed runs, common SGR sampling under -R, filename presentation and explicit charset/alias precedence. Detection and filename questions share one typed policy. Other charsets/custom definitions, locale validity, nonstandard UTF-8 scalar forms and other color-safe controls remain open. Binary sampling shares SGR grammar with display but preserves the 668 quirk that skips the initial ESC before its OSC-prefix recognizer; both unsupported OSC and OSC 8 payload controls still trigger the question.

entries.title: Numeric command overflow pauses safely and resumes the pending command
entries.evidence: compatible in the named tested scenarios
entries.cause: An unsigned-size prefix reached unchecked row arithmetic and panicked. Prefixes now retain signed-64 overflow state until command dispatch, show the modal oracle error and preserve startup remainders. Startup quit/resume/long input and interactive recovery match, including the redundant top-jump bell. Candidate-only safety also covers large legal position arithmetic. Other jump targets and out-of-file seek diagnostics remain open in S07.
